intent: Prevent a MaxActivationDuration configuration change from orphaning a non-terminal siren execution or its physical compensation by reconstructing and routing exact historical duration-derived execution bundles across restart.
invariants: A siren execution that has enabled a physical device remains routable to its exact persisted plan after process restart even when MaxActivationDuration changes.

Historical siren plan versions are reconstructed only from the canonical version form 1-<positive Go duration> and the recompiled PlanID, PlanVersion and PlanDigest must exactly match persisted identity.
Unknown, malformed or digest-mismatched non-terminal siren execution identity fails Open or preflight closed.
New siren executions start only on the currently configured duration bundle.
Drive and Stop select the engine matching the persisted execution digest before advance or cancellation.
Cancellation of a historical execution retains access to its compensation stack and SirenEnsureDisabled handler.
The shared Axiom Store and Host remain the durable execution authority; Home Sentinel does not fork or duplicate the workflow kernel.
Configuration change never silently rewrites an existing siren execution into the active plan.
contracts: plan version encoding is canonical and reversible to MaxActivationDuration
reconstructed historical plan digest exactly equals the persisted digest before registration
Axiom Host registers active and reconstructed historical siren engines over the existing Production Store
service Start explicitly uses the active bundle and preserves same-execution idempotency
service Drive, Stop and non-terminal Get validate and route by persisted bundle identity
Serve validates persisted siren executions before starting Host coordinator/worker and the active schedule runner
terminal historical executions do not block startup but non-terminal unknown identities do
resourceguard still fences conflicting physical ownership across executions independent of bundle version
acceptance_evidence: Pebble test enables a siren under duration A, closes the process, reopens the same store under different duration B, cancels/drives the old execution through its historical engine and proves the siren is disabled by compensation
old execution retains duration-A PlanVersion/PlanDigest while a new execution after reopen uses duration B
historical cancellation does not duplicate the original enable and compensation applies exactly once semantically
malformed historical version is rejected fail-closed
valid version with mismatched persisted digest is rejected fail-closed
canonical duration parser rejects zero, negative and non-canonical aliases
existing automatic safety timer and manual-stop tests remain green
Gremlins produces non-empty siren orchestration evidence with no lived/not-covered/timeout critical blockers
